A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RealUID research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: V2 reports original CIFAR-10 and CelebA experiments, coefficient ablations, convergence measurements, and a diffusion-model SiD study in Section 4 and Appendices A.3 and D.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and their reported FID scores, convergence curves, efficiency measurements, and generated samples.

M1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a general Bregman-divergence inverse-distillation objective family. This is a formal objective extension; the operational RealUID algorithm and the previously proposed mixed-data DMD objective and updates remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain conditional and unconditional CIFAR-10 generation, CelebA generation, the CIFAR-10 SiD study, and Gaussian illustrations. The new discussion of discrete-time bridge models does not introduce an evaluated task.

E2.justification: The controlled UID/FGM and UID+GAN comparisons, appendix SiD comparisons, and comparator sets in Tables 3–5 are retained. ReFlow's citation changes to the publication of the same work; the newly cited RSD method is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 changes the stated CIFAR-10 distillation budget from 400,000 to 500,000 gradient updates. The FID evaluation procedure and separately stated fine-tuning budgets remain unchanged. This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The coefficient and GAN-weight sweeps, fine-tuning analyses, convergence comparisons, Gaussian teacher-corruption illustrations, and SiD stability study are retained. Their evidence in Tables 1 and 6–8 and Figures 2–6 is unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain three independent FID evaluation runs, the stated empirical variance below 0.01, and inference-time averaging over 10,000 iterations in Appendix D.1 and Table 5. No new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Reported training durations change: CelebA's 800,000/1,600,000-update runs take approximately 5/10 days in v4 versus 4.5/9 days in v2; CIFAR-10 changes from 4.5 to 5 days alongside its revised budget. FID results, inference benchmarks, curves, and samples remain unchanged, including RealUID's 1.98/1.87 in Table 2 and 0.89 in Table 8.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 replaces the functional-derivative proof with a KL-loss min-max derivation connecting DMD to inverse optimization (v4 Equations 37–39), while retaining Lemma 5's final mixed-data gradient. It also introduces a Bregman-divergence definition and general linearization-based distillation construction, substantially broadening the theoretical account.

C1.justification: Section 5 changes DMD from explicitly outside UID to a special case using a KL-based loss. The abstract and introduction retain the central claims of unifying matching-model distillation and incorporating real data without an additional GAN.

C2.justification: V4 removes the assertion that unequal DMD coefficients cause total generator collapse and instead explains the single-coefficient construction through KL-loss linearity. Appendix C.3 newly states applicability to discrete-time bridge models. Existing qualifications about heuristic SiD settings remain.

D1.justification: Appendices D.1 and D.3 revise training-budget and wall-clock documentation and clarify that both generator and fake model use the stated Adam settings. Hardware, initialization, other implementation details, and code/checkpoint access information are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations to Augmented Bridge Matching by De Bortoli et al. and Residual Shifting Distillation by Selikhanovych et al., and repositions DMD within inverse distillation. Other reference changes largely update or consolidate citations to the same works.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized wording edits in the abstract and background and retitles and reorganizes Appendix A.5 around inverse optimization. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact; some apparent changes are relocated figure-associated discussion.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 and Table 2 move within the main text, appendix figures shift relative to surrounding discussion, and Algorithm 1 now shares a page with its introduction. The eight tables and fifteen figures retain their designs and content; changes primarily concern placement and spacing.

improvement.justification: V4 improves theoretical coherence by deriving DMD through the paper's inverse-optimization principle and recovering the existing mixed-data gradient more directly. Its coefficient argument and Bregman extension strengthen this account. Empirical evidence remains unchanged, while the budget and runtime revisions are not identified as corrections or reruns, so the supported overall gain is limited.
